subject: physics
question_text: What is the acceleration of a projectile at the top of its trajectory?

verification.note: Sri Chaitanya IPE Junior Fastrack (Rev. May 2024), VERY SHORT ANSWER 7 of Unit 4. The mark split is invented and needs a Telangana IPE teacher; no exam appearance years are printed for Unit 4, so appearances[] stays empty.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The answer
lines: At the top of the path,
steps.margin_note: Give the direction with the value — "g" alone is half an answer.
steps.why: Gravity is the only force on a projectile, at the top exactly as everywhere else on the path.
common_mistakes: Answering zero because the vertical VELOCITY is zero there.

recall.must_convey: That the acceleration is g, directed vertically downward.

steps.label: The reason
lines: The vertical VELOCITY is zero at the
top, but gravity acts throughout the
steps.margin_note: Name the trap out loud: velocity zero does not mean acceleration zero.
steps.why: The top is special for the velocity, not for the force. Nothing switches off at the peak — that is why the path bends back down.
common_mistakes: Confusing the zero vertical velocity with zero acceleration.

recall.must_convey: That the vertical velocity is zero at the top but gravity still acts.
accept: velocity is zero but not acceleration
